items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: After Harry James, you know; there's one thing about James. He took and played the whole tune for you.

ctx.x: And he had it all planned. And this was fine; however, after about three, four weeks or maybe six weeks or so, his lip is in pretty good shape. Now he wants the third parts.

Now, trumpet players in those days, you -- you know that these kids during the war, they got to be -- before the war they got to be fantastic. They had guys like Louis Armstrong to look back on. Now they were fluffing him off, and Harry James, those guys were getting passé. These kids were coming along and they could play twice as high and probably twice as fast, and they had fantastic commands of their instruments, and the only thing that they worried about, most of them being 4-Fs, is the fact that they'd be…
